Lonhro was foaled on 10 December 1998 at Woodlands Stud, Denman, New South Wales.
He was a dark bay stallion by Octagonal out of the mare Shadea (by Straight Strike).
Lonhro won 26 races from 35 starts, including 11 Group 1 victories.
His most famous wins include the Caulfield Cup (2001), Queen Elizabeth Stakes (2002, 2003), George Main Stakes (2001–2003), and Chipping Norton Stakes (2002, 2003).
He earned over A$8.9 million in prizemoney, making him one of Australia's highest-earning racehorses at the time of his retirement.
Lonhro was Australian Champion Racehorse of the Year in 2003–04.
He was known for his aggressive racing style, often looking back at rivals and surging away when challenged.
The famous 'That's racing!' moment occurred after his 2003 George Main Stakes win when trainer John Hawkes responded to a heckler.
Lonhro received a guard of honour at Rosehill Gardens on his final race day (10 April 2004) – one of the most emotional farewells in Australian racing.
He raced successfully from age two through to age six, showing exceptional longevity at elite level.
Lonhro was trained by John Hawkes and ridden by Darren Beadman for most of his major victories.
Many racing experts consider him one of the greatest middle-distance horses in modern Australian racing history.
After retirement, he stood at stud at Woodlands Stud and later Arrowfield Stud, siring multiple stakes winners including Denman and Pierro.
Lonhro developed a huge public following; fans travelled interstate just to watch him race.
He was inducted into the Australian Racing Hall of Fame in 2014.
